full_judgment:
2. The case of the petitioner is that the respondent No. 3 Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited, represented by Assistant Vice President, Islami Bank Bangladesh Ltd. Faridpur Branch, Faridpur as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 14 of 2002 in the Court of Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Faridpur for realisation of Taka 30,20,428 against the defendant-petitioner and two others. The said Title Suit No. 14 of 2002 was decreed ex parte on 10-3-2003 and accordingly, the preliminary decree was signed on 15-3-2003. The respondent No. 3 without filing any application for final decree as per mandatory provision of Order XXXIV, rule 5(3) of the Civil Procedure Code, filed the Decree Execution Case No. 18 of 2003 which was subsequently renumbered as Execution Case No. 30 of 2004 and the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Faridpur, most illegally started execution proceedings against the petitioner which is liable to be declared to have been proceeded without any lawful authority. Against the illegal proceeding of Execution Case No. 30 of 2004 the petitioner previously filed Writ Petition No. 3203 of 2005 which was heard and disposed of with a direction upon the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Faridpur, to dispose of the execution Case having regard to the provision of Order XXXIV, rule 4(1) of the Civil Procedure Code and section 5(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 but the Artha Rin Adalat without complying the direction of the Humble High Court Division and without considering the provision of law passed the impugned order for taking possession of the mortgaged property which is illegal, arbitrary and liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority. 

 3. The petitioner further stated that the Title Suit No. 14 of 2002 was a mortgage suit and the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat passed a preliminary decree on 15-3-2003 and thereafter, without passing the final decree, has started the Execution Case No. 30 of 2004 against the petitioner which is not lawful. 

 5. The respondent No. 3 Bank has con-tested the suit by filing affidavit-in-opposition alleging that the petitioner was sanctioned an amount of Taka 25 lac on 1-8-1998. Subsequently, the loan amount was enhanced to Taka 33 lac for a period of 1 year. The petitioner failed to repay the said loan as per agreement. In such circumstances the Bank filed the aforesaid Title Suit No. 14 of 2002 for realization of Taka 30,20,428 as stood on 31-12-2001. The learned Court passed ex parte decree on 10-3-2003 and directed the petitioner to pay the said decretal amount within 60 days from the date. Thereafter the respondent No. 3 filed Execution Case No. 18 of 2003 which was subsequently renumbered as Execution Case No. 30 of 2004. On 3-11-2003 the judgment debt (petitioner) appeared in execution case by filing Vokalatnama and promised to re-pay the loan. The petitioner neither filed any appeal nor any application under section 19 of the Artha Rin Ain, 2003 for setting aside the ex parte decree. The petitioner also did not file any application before the Execution Court for drawing up final decree before proceeding with the execution case. The decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat is a simple money decree and that the provision of section 5(3) of the Artha Rin Ain, 2003 is applicable in case of mortgage suit for foreclosure but no final decree is required when a simple money decree is passed. 

 6. Mr AKM Shamsul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submitted that the Artha Rin Adalat passed a preliminary decree on 10-3-2003 and decree was signed on 15-3-2003 and thereafter the respondent bank without making any prayer for final decree started the execution case for realisation of the decretal amount which is contrary to the provision of section 5(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Mr Shamsul Haque thereafter submitted that the petitioner previously filed Writ Petition No. 3203 of 2005 before this Court and this Court directed the Artha Rin Adalat to proceed with the execution case as per provision of Order XXXIV, rule 4(1) of the Civil Procedure Code and section 5(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, but the Artha Rin Adalat without complying with the direction of the High Court Division and without following the said provision of law illegally has been proceeding with the execution case which is illegal and liable to be declared void and without lawful authority. Mr Shamsul Haque further submitted that the order dated 11-9-2005 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat for delivery of possession of the mortgaged property in favour of the bank without following the provision of law and without drawing up final decree, is illegal, ultra virus and the same is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority 

 7. Mr Md Golam Mostafa, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 3 Bank submitted that the Title Suit 14 of 2002 filed by the Bank was a simple suit for realization of money and the Court passed the money decree on 10-3-2003 and from the language of the said decree it would be evident that the said decree was a simple money decree and, as such, final decree is not required to be drawn up before selling the mortgaged property in auction. Mr Golam Mostafa also submitted that the decree was passed on 10-3-2003 and Execution Case No. 30 of 2004 was started when the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 came into force on 1-5-2003 and as per provision of section 5(4) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 no final decree is necessary before selling the mortgaged property in auction and the Court rightly passed the impugned order. 

 8. The case of the petitioner is, that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 14 of 2002 was a mortgaged suit and, as such, without drawing up final decree the proceeding of the execution case is not maintainable. Since, the Artha Rin Adalat has been proceeding with the execution case, the petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 3203 of 2005 before the High Court Division. This Court disposed of the Writ petition summarily on 15-5-2005 with a direction to the Artha Rin Adalat to dispose of the execution case as per provision of Order XXXIV, rule 4(1) of the Civil Procedure Code and section 5(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Thereafter, the petitioner applied to the Artha Rin Adalat to follow the observation made by the High Court Division in proceeding with the execution case. 

 9. The petitioner has challenged two orders in this Writ petition. From order No. 26 dated 12-2-2005 it appears that the petitioner prayed for time to deposit the rest decrial amount and the decree holder filed an application under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat to issue a certificate vesting the mortgage property in the possession of the the bank. The Artha Rin Adalat allowed the application filed by the decree holder and rejected the application filed by the petitioner to allow him time to deposit the decretal amount. By order No. 40 dated 11-9-2005 the Court directed to issue writ for delivery of possession to deliver the possession of the mortgaged property in favour of the bank. From these two orders it does not appear that the petitioner made any prayer before the Executing Court for proceeding with the Execution case as per direction of the High Court Division passed in Writ Petition No. 3203 of 2005. Though the basis of whole argument of the petitioner is that the Artha Rin Adalat failed to comply with the direction of the High Court Division. 

 10. The learned Advocate for the respondent No. 3 has filed the photocopy of the certified copy of the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 14 of 2002. From the said ex parte decree it appears that the decree was a simple money decree. The ordering portion of the said decree reads as under: 

 11. The Title Suit No. 14 of 2002 was a suit for realization of outstanding dues and the court has passed the simple money decree. The suit was not registered as mortgage suit and the Court has not passed the preliminary decree. The decree passed in the aforesaid suit to be considered as a decree passed under sub-section 4 of section 5 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and as soon as the auction sale will be completed against mortgaged loan of immovable property the preliminary decree to be considered as final decree. Section 5(4) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 reads as follows : 

 12. The aforesaid decree for realization of money was passed on 10-3-2003 as per provision of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990. The Execution Case No. 30 of 2004 was filed when the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 came into effect. From saving clause of section 60(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 it appears that the proceeding which were filed under the Artha Rin Ain 1990 but proceeded when the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 came into force, shall proceed as per provision of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 as far as it practical. So form this provision we find that the execution case has been proceeding in accordance with law. It does not appear from the impugned orders that the petitioner filed any application before the executing Court bringing allegation that the execution case has not been proceeded as per direction of the High Court Division passed in the aforesaid writ petition. We do not find any substance in this writ petition to interfere with the impugned order.
